title: Nonparametric Estimation of the Diffusion-Interaction Function in Particle Systems
summary: We study the problem of nonparametric estimation of the interaction function in particle systems whose interaction enters through the diffusion coefficient. The particle system is observed discretely over a fixed time interval, and the interaction function is assumed to belong to a suitable nonparametric function class. We propose an estimation procedure based on empirical risk minimization over finite-dimensional sieve spaces, introducing a computable contrast function that exploits the local volatility of the observed trajectories.
